overview:
Wisconsin's 5th District, covering Milwaukee's western suburbs, is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, with a partisan lean of about eleven points toward the GOP. Scott Fitzgerald, the incumbent and former state Senate majority leader, is running for reelection with a large financial advantage.

His Democratic challenger, Andrew Beck, has raised roughly fifteen thousand dollars and has minimal cash on hand, while Fitzgerald reports over 1.3 million dollars raised. No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets give the Democrat only about a four percent chance of winning. The fundamentals, money, and district lean all point in the same direction, making this a Safe Republican seat with little realistic prospect of an upset.
